studies.label: Experiment I (teams: human-only vs single-AI vs multiple-AI)
studies.cluster_se_treatment: Teams were randomized to AI conditions (PDF p. 9). Regressions analyze repeated team-task outputs and report robust SEs without stating team clustering (PDF pp. 37-39, Appendix B, Tables 1-3). Bayesian models have no reported team random effects (PDF p. 40). Cluster counts are analyzed teams printed in Appendix A, Table 1 (PDF p. 34), not people.

arms.name: Human-only team
arms.description: Team worked without AI on analyzed outputs. A single ChatGPT4.0 touchpoint was offered after submission for refinement, but refinement effects were excluded (PDF p. 9, footnote 4).

arms.name: Single-AI team

arms.name: Multiple-AI team

studies.task: Each team wrote articles about college students’ job hunting and career development and developed a digital transformation strategy for a traditional retail chain (PDF pp. 9-10).

estimates.measure_detail: Six independent online-panel judges rated each team-task output, blind to hypotheses and conditions, on a scale from one to ten (PDF p. 10, Section 2.1). The analysis uses one score per team-task output; the rater-score aggregation formula is not specified.

regression.model: OLS on team-task outputs; task fixed effects and standardized baseline team age, gender, education, IQ, prior AI use, size and familiarity. Human-only reference for AI-versus-control; single-AI reference for AI-design.

sources.quote: enhancement in overall quality when AI is utilized (β = 0.417, p < .01), explaining additional 3.7% variance in performance.

estimates.notes: The randomized unit is the team. Each team contributes repeated task outputs; robust SEs are reported without team clustering or team random effects. SE basis is output. Printed regression N is n_units, not people. Analyzed headcounts are unreported. Coefficients are in raw rating-scale units: only control variables were standardized (PDF pp. 10-11). No combined-AI descriptive mean or SD is printed; neither was computed. Confidence-interval endpoints are only graphical in Figure 3 (PDF p. 28); none were read from the figure. Overall quality is coded usefulness, not overall creativity. paper_effect.type=other records the additional variance explained exactly in the printed percent units. It is a model-fit change, not a signed standardized mean difference, and has not been converted to a fraction.

The citation record confirms the local arXiv version, but not chronology relative to an inaccessible SSRN revision.

notes: Reconciled on 2026-10-11. Read all 92689 characters of the markdown in contiguous chunks through the end of Appendix B; checked cited PDF pages with pymupdf, including the arm-descriptive, OLS and Bayesian tables. The original printed decimal precision and signs are preserved in source quotations. No effects, headcounts, output totals, pooled means, SDs or graphical endpoints were computed. All scripted field disagreements are resolved in resolutions; repeated n_units entries in the diff are represented once per unique slug and field. Additional omitted sd_level and study country/shared_sample differences are resolved explicitly. Agreed-field audit: PDF pp. 8-11 and 26 establish a laboratory between-team randomized design, randomized people counts, and AI available during output production; PDF p. 34 distinguishes analyzed teams from task outputs and does not print analyzed headcounts. Study and arm n_analyzed and every estimate n_treatment/n_control/n_total remain null. Repeated tasks do not constitute a within-person crossover: within_person is null throughout. All outcomes answer with_ai, outcome_with_ai is true, timing is immediate, and higher_is is more_creative. Overall quality and usefulness are usefulness; novelty is novelty (PDF p. 10; codebook section 6). Units and SD levels are output, not individual people or rater observations. Main pooled-task OLS and Bayesian uncertainty is output-level because clustering on the randomized teams is not stated; task-specific descriptors have no reported contrast uncertainty. The three eligible S1 screening outcomes each have all four main arm contrasts, plus the printed task-specific descriptors and dependent Bayesian/expanded-model variants. All six S2 individual-versus-team screening contrasts are explicitly excluded as nonrandom. Relative rating-score distributions do not measure content diversity across people. The full-document audit found no additional eligible outcome or contrast omitted by both extractors; n_added is 0. Retained all three A-only coefficients as alternate estimates of the original randomized team contrast; their joint fit also uses the nonrandom individual cohort and must not count as independent evidence. Text/table Bayesian variants are also dependent, conflicting reports, not independent effects. The reported additional variance explained remains in percent under paper_effect.type=other, and inverse Bayes factors are identified under test.type=other. Posterior SDs remain in source quotations and are not relabeled as outcome SDs or frequentist SEs. The external supplement remains inaccessible. Page locators are one-based PDF pages; figure and appendix pages have no printed numerical pagination.
